units.verbatim_section_rubric: *At the Liturgy: the Beatitudes, Ode 3 on 4, and of the Cross, Ode 6 on 4; Troparion of the Cross, of the Saint; Glory, Kontakion of the Saint; and now, Kontakion of the Cross. Prokeimenon, Tone 2: "Save, O Lord, Thy people"; verse: "Unto Thee, O Lord..." And the other Prokeimenon for the Saints. Epistle for the Cross, lection 125 [1 Cor. 1:18–24]; and of the Saints, lection to All Saints [Heb. 11:33–40]. Alleluia, Tone 1: "Remember Thy congregation..." [Ps. 73:2]; verse: "God is our King..." [Ps. 73:12]; and the other: "The righteous cried..." [Ps. 33:18]. Gospel for the Cross, from John, lection 60 [John 19:6–11, 13–20, 25–28, 30–35]; and Gospel for the Saints, lection to All Saints [Matt. 10:32–33, 37–38; 19:27–30]. Communion Hymn: "The light of Thy countenance is signed upon us" [Ps. 4:7]; another: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous" [Ps. 32:1].*[^473] [^474]

units.slavonic_incipit: възѣмае чт҃ное древо съ блюдомь на
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: въземае чтное древо с блюдом на гла ву
units.slavonic_diplomatic: възѣмае чт҃ное древо съ блюдомь на гла вꙋ . и исходит лѣвою страною . из олтаря прѣидꙋщима двѣма свѣщиама великима с кадиломь . приходи же до цр҃ьскыхъ вра . и тꙋ стоить ѡжидаꙗ коньца тр҃тмꙋ . кончанꙋ жетр҃тмꙋ . д іако . в ъзгла . п рꙋдрость про сти . браіа поют ро . псн ги люди своꙗ . г лю щее дїногажы . и приходи . ерен носѧ чт҃ное древо . прѣ ст҃ыа двери . пробготованꙋ столꙋ и положн его връхъ стола . и кади . пробгото вамѣ водѣ в чаши . п ое тры : цїніюі сщ҃іае ерен водо . посщ҃инии водѣ . и покропленино сщенныꙗ воды . стваряе поклоненіе чт҃нома дрѣвꙋ . ѡ чино . г м пе поста п осе ѡ кт҃еа .
units.english_cohort_translation: *He takes up the Precious Wood with the dish upon his head, and goes forth by the northern side out of the altar, two great candles going before him with a censer; and he comes unto the Royal Doors, and there stands awaiting the conclusion of the Trisagion. And the Trisagion being concluded, the deacon proclaims: "Wisdom! Stand upright!" The brethren chant the troparion: "Save, O Lord, Thy people," chanting it once. And the priest comes, bearing the Precious Wood, before the Holy Doors to a prepared table, and lays it upon the table, and censes. Water having been prepared in a vessel, troparia are chanted in order; the priest blesses the water. After the blessing of the water and the sprinkling of the sanctified water, he makes veneration to the Precious Wood, in ordinary order, bowing down thrice; after this, litany, dismissal.*[^475]

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: еи оуспение прты бца пра знуем ве
units.slavonic_diplomatic: е҃і Оуспеніе пртыꙗ бца . пра знꙋемь ве дн҃ь . пѣніекъсенощное . на ма лои вечерни . стры праз на д҃ сл҃ і н сагл҃ны праз . на сти праз . тро гл҃а а҃ . Въ ржтвѣ двыство , съхранила еси . въ оуспеніи мли ра не ѡставила еси бце . преставлена къ животоу . мт҃не щи живота . мл҃твами тво ими избавляеши ѡт съмр҃ти дш҃а нша :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* In giving birth Thou didst preserve Thy virginity; in falling asleep Thou didst not forsake the world, O Mother of God. Thou hast passed over unto life, being the Mother of Life, and by Thy prayers Thou dost deliver our souls from death!

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: чтеа г празникову на исхожение
units.slavonic_diplomatic: чт҃еа г҃ . празникову . На исхоженіе . само гл҃ны . г҃ . гл҃а а҃ . и гл҃а в҃ . и гл҃а г҃ . слава гл҃а е҃ . прте празнослюбци . і н҃ . въспоите лїе . На сти самогл҃нь гл҃а д҃ . сти же гли въскр҃ни гни въ покои твои . клѧт ся гь да выдови . сл҃а і ны гл҃ д҃ . егда изыде бце по тр҃толь . тр҃о празни . г лется г жвы .

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: г ж обыное стисловие на многомлтивы
units.slavonic_diplomatic: г ж҃ . ѡбыное ст҃исловіе . На многомл҃тивы т҃ѣ празни . сте гл҃а д҃ . про гл҃ д҃ . помѧ ноу имя твое . сти . слыши дщи . всѧко дыханіе . єѵліе ѡ лоу . въ ѡ врема , въ ставши маріаль . стра . празни . гл҃а . ѕ҃ .
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion of the feast thrice. Ordinary psalmody [Kathismata]. At the Polyeleos: Sessional hymns of the feast. Gradual, Tone 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "I will remember Thy name" [Ps. 44:18]; verse: "Give ear, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear" [Ps. 44:11]. "Let every breath..." Gospel from Luke [1:39–49, 56]: "In those days, Mary arose..." Sticheron of the feast, Tone 6: "When the passing..." Two canons: of master Cosmas [Tone 1] and of master John [Tone 4]; heirmoi twice, and troparia on 12; afterwards the heirmos of both canons both choirs together once. After Ode 3, Hypakoe: "All generations shall call thee blessed." After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 2.*

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в млтвах неоусыпающую бцю и в за
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Въ мл҃твахъ неоусыпающꙋю бц҃ю · и въ за стꙋпленіе непрелагаемое оупованіе · гробъ и оумрътвіе неоудържаста · ꙗкоже бо живота мт҃рь на животъ прѣстави · иже въ оутробꙋ въселивыисѧ приснодѣвьственꙋю :~ На ѳ҃ ·
units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of the Falling Asleep of the Most Holy Theotokos [Tone 2]:*[^479] In prayers the sleepless Mother of God, and in intercessions an unfailing hope, neither the grave nor death could hold; for as the Mother of Life, He Who dwelt in Her ever-virgin womb translated Her unto life!

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *At Ode 9, candles are given to the brethren. "More honorable" we do not sing. Exapostilarion of the feast thrice. On the Praises, we sing 3 of the feast, Tone 4, on 6; Glory, and now, Tone 6: "On Thine immortal..." Great Doxology. Troparion of the feast; litany, dismissal; and holy oil is given to the brethren.*

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сл и нн празн на оутр тро
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Сл҃ і нн҃ празн҃ · на оутр҃ тро празн҃ · в҃ · сл҃а оубрꙋ · і нн҃ празн҃ · сѣ праз ка ѡбразꙋ с їрм҃ль на ѕ҃ · праз на д҃ · и с҃ на д҃ · по г҃ пѣ ко҃ праз · по ѕ҃ ко҃ оубрꙋ гл҃ в҃ ·
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion of the Holy Mandylion:* We venerate Thy most pure Icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, to deliver them whom Thou hadst created from the bondage of the enemy. Therefore thankfully we cry unto Thee: Having filled all things with joy, O our tender-hearted Savior, Who didst come to save the world!
units.slavonic_text: Сл҃ і нн҃ празн҃ · на оутр҃ тро празн҃ · в҃ · сл҃а оубрꙋ · і нн҃ празн҃ · сѣ праз ка ѡбразꙋ с їрм҃ль на ѕ҃ · праз на д҃ · и с҃ на д҃ · по г҃ пѣ ко҃ праз · по ѕ҃ ко҃ оубрꙋ гл҃ в҃ ·
units.english_text: *Troparion of the Holy Mandylion:* We venerate Thy most pure Icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, to deliver them whom Thou hadst created from the bondage of the enemy. Therefore thankfully we cry unto Thee: Having filled all things with joy, O our tender-hearted Savior, Who didst come to save the world!

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source:
тр҃о гл҃а в҃ · Прч҃томоу ѡбразꙋ покланꙗ
емьсѧ бл҃гыи · просѧще прощениꙗ прегрѣше
ніемъ нашимъ х҃е б҃е · волею бо изволилъ
еси възити на кр҃тъ · да избавиши ѿ работы
вражіа ꙗже созда · тѣмь бл҃годарѧще вопіемъ ти
радости исполнивыи всѧ бл҃госерде сп҃се нашъ · прише
дыи сп҃сти миръ :~ Сл҃ і нн҃ празн҃ · на оутр҃ тро
празн҃ · в҃ · сл҃а оубрꙋ · і нн҃ празн҃ · сѣ праз
ка ѡбразꙋ с їрм҃ль на ѕ҃ · праз на д҃ · и с҃
на д҃ · по г҃ пѣ ко҃ праз · по ѕ҃ ко҃ оубрꙋ гл҃ в҃ ·

units.slavonic_diplomatic: С҃тго пр҃рка самоила · пѣніе в коу · тр҃о · пр҃о рока твоего · глас а҃ · сл҃а і нн҃ празн҃ · кѡ҃ с҃тго гл҃а г҃ · Ꙗко драгыи и чт҃ныи дарь · пре же зачатна въ данъ бы[сть] · и з млада томоу ꙗко аг҃глъ послоуживъ всеблажене и сподобн сѧ бꙋдꙋщаꙗ вѣщати · тѣмь въпіемъ ти радоусѧ пр҃рче бж҃іи самоиле · архїерѣю ве ликыи :~

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *The Holy Apostle Thaddaeus, and the Martyr Bassa [August 21]. The Holy Martyr Agathonicus [August 22]: on that day is chanted according to the weekly tone [of the Oktoechos]; Stichera of both on 4 of the Saint; and now, of the feast; on the Aposticha, all of the feast; Troparion... ..."Thy martyrs, O Lord..." Glory, and now, of the feast. At Matins: Troparion of the feast twice; Glory, of the Saint; And now, of the feast. Sessional hymns of the feast. Canon of the feast on 6, and of the Saints two [canons]. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "The angelic choir":*[^488]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: кано празн҃ на ѕ҃ · и с҃ты два · по г҃ · пѣ кѡ҃ с҃ты гл҃а д҃ · ликъ аг҃гльскыи · Званіе бл҃го стажавъ бг҃омꙋдре · мꙋже лꙋкавы ѿвратилъ еси не вѣры · неоубоꙗвсѧ мꙋкъ ·
units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of the Holy Martyr Agathonicus:* Having acquired a noble calling, O divinely-wise one, thou didst turn deceitful men from unbelief, fearing no torments, O glorious Agathonicus; therefore thou hast become an inheritor of good things, and hast received with those who suffered with thee a worthy crown!

units.verbatim_book_heading: PART III: MENOLOGION :: At Matins
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *Katabasia: "I shall open my mouth," both choirs together. After Ode 3, Sessional hymn of the feast; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos. At Ode 9, "More honorable" we do not recite in psalmody. Exapostilarion of the feast twice. On the Praises, we sing 3 of the feast, Tone 4, on 4; Glory, and now, Tone 6: "On Thine immortal..." Great Doxology. Troparion of the feast; litany, catechetical instruction, dismissal. At the Liturgy: of the feast, from both canons both 9th Odes with heirmoi on 8; Troparion of the feast; Glory, and now, Kontakion of the feast; Prokeimenon, Alleluia, Communion Hymn of the feast; and Epistle and Gospel of the day.*

units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of the Holy Apostle Eutyches:* *Troparion and Prokeimenon... units.english_cohort_translation: *Exapostilarion. On the Praises, of the Forerunner on 4; Glory, Tone 6: "Again Herod..."; And now, Theotokion. Great Doxology. Troparion of the Forerunner; litany, dismissal; and holy oil is given to the brethren from the lamp of the Saint. At the Liturgy: for the Forerunner, Ode 3 and Ode 6. Prokeimenon: "The righteous shall rejoice" [Ps. 63:11]; Verse: "Hear my voice, O God" [Ps. 63:2]. Epistle from the Acts [13:25–32]: "In those days, as John fulfilled his course..." Alleluia: "The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree" [Ps. 91:13]. Gospel from Mark [6:14–30]: "At that time, Herod heard of Jesus..." Communion Hymn: "In everlasting memory [shall the righteous be]" [Ps. 111:6].*[^499]

units.english_cohort_translation: *On Saturday evening: "Blessed is the man." On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 10: 3 Resurrectional, and 4 Anatolian, and in the Triodion two, in Tone 1, twice; Glory, in the Triodion; Both now, Resurrectional. The sequence of the Saint in the Menaion is sung at Compline. On the Aposticha, Resurrectional and alphabetical stichera. At Matins: the ordinary psalmody [Kathismata], and the Polyeleos ["Many-merciful"]; Graduals of the tone; Prokeimenon; "Let every breath [praise the Lord]"; Sunday Gospel; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50; Resurrectional Sticheron. Canons: Resurrectional on 4, and of the Theotokos on 4, and in the Triodion on 6. After Ode 3, Sessional hymn in the Triodion. After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 2:*"[^506]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: На ѳ҃ · пѣ ст҃ыхъ · свѣ въскр҃сень · и в трїѡ · на хва ст҃рыі · на и҃ · славословіе великое · нача сѣхъ · гл҃етсѧ тр҃о · въскр҃ень · и кѡ҃ · въ трїѡ · на лѵ҃тоургіи · бл҃жена · въ ѡ҃ · ап҃л жен еѵ҃ліе · наставшее · сед҃ н҃е · Подобае т же вѣдати · ꙗко въ тꙋ н҃елю постатсѧ про клѧтіи арменове · сквернакаго своего поста гл҃емаго арциоу҃рци · мы же на всѧкъ днь ·

units.english_cohort_translation: *On Saturday evening: "Blessed is the man." Stichera on 10: 3 Resurrectional, and 3 Anatolian, and in the Triodion two Idiomela, twice; Glory, in the Triodion; Both now, Resurrectional. At the Entrance: Prokeimenon. units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of the Prodigal Son [Tone 3]:* Having foolishly fled from Thy paternal glory, in evils I have squandered the riches Thou gavest unto me; therefore I offer unto Thee the voice of the prodigal: I have sinned before Thee, O compassionate Father; receive me repenting, and make me as one of Thy hired servants![^512]

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: At Small Vespers: Stichera of the Forerunner on 4; Glory, and now, of the Forerunner; on the Aposticha, of the Forerunner
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On Friday evening: Stichera on 6: 3 of the Martyrs of the incoming tone, and in the Triodion stichera 3; Glory: "I weep and I lament"; Both now, Theotokion 1 of the incoming tone. In place of the Prokeimenon, at Vespers: Alleluia, in Tone 8; Verse: "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken [unto Thyself, O Lord]; and their memorial is from generation to generation" [Ps. 64:5; 101:13]. On the Aposticha: one of the Martyrs, and for the reposed two Idiomela of the current tone; Glory, Tone 6: "A beginning today is composed..."; Both now, in the Triodion: "Thou art our God." Troparion, Tone 8: "Who by depth of wisdom..."; Glory, both now, Theotokion. Canon in the Octoechos on 6, and in the Triodion on 8. On the Praises, in the Triodion on 4. On the Aposticha, at Matins. At the Liturgy, in the Triodion: Ode 3 and Ode 6. Prokeimenon: "Their souls shall dwell among good things" [Ps. 24:13]; [Verse:] "Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul" [Ps. 24:1]. Epistles: The daily one: "Brethren, all things are lawful unto me..." [1 Cor. 6:12–20]; The other for the reposed: "Brethren, I would not have you to be ignorant..." [1 Thess. 4:13–17]. Alleluia: "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken." Gospel: the daily one [Luke 21:8–9, 25–27, 33–36], and for the reposed [John 5:24–30]. Communion Hymn: "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen."*[^514]

Prokeimenon: "Great is our Lord, and great is His power" [Ps. 146:5]; [Verse:] "Praise ye the Lord" [Ps. 146:1]. Epistle to the Corinthians: "Brethren, meat commends us not to God..." [1 Cor. 8:8–9:2]. Alleluia: "O come, let us rejoice in the Lord" [Ps. 94:1]; [Verse:] "Let us come before His presence" [Ps. 94:2]. Gospel from Matthew [25:31–46]: "The Lord said: When the Son of man shall come..." Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens" [Ps. 148:1]; and the other: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous" [Ps. 32:1].*[^519]

On the Aposticha, the Octoechos is not sung; there is sung the daily Automelon 2 and 4, in the same Tone 5, once, both choirs together; Glory, both now, Theotokion. Thus sings the stichera at Vespers during the other days of Cheesefare week. But let it be known that on Cheesefare Saturday and Sunday the Menaion is not sung, but the sequence of the Saints whose memory is accounted... ...accounted on Saturday and Sunday is sung at Compline, or whenever the ecclesiarch wills.*[^521]

units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of Cheesefare Sunday [Tone 6]:* Instructor of wisdom and Giver of prudence, Educator of the senseless and Defender of the poor: confirm and give understanding unto my heart, O Master! Do Thou give me the word, O Word of wisdom; for lo, I will not refrain both my lips from crying unto Thee: O Merciful One, have mercy on me who am fallen![^528]

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On the Praises, on 8: Resurrectional on 4, and in the Triodion on 4. Great Doxology. At the Liturgy: the Octoechos on 6... ...and in the Triodion, Ode 6 on 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 8: "Make vows, and pay them unto the Lord our God" [Ps. 75:12]; [Verse:] "In Judah is God known" [Ps. 75:2]. Epistle to the Romans: "Brethren, now is our salvation nearer than when we believed..." [Rom. 13:11–14:4]. Alleluia: "It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord" [Ps. 91:2]; [Verse:] "For the Lord is upright" [Ps. 91:16]. Gospel from Matthew [6:14–21]: "The Lord said: If ye forgive men their trespasses..." And the rest of the Divine Liturgy of John Chrysostom is celebrated. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens" [Ps. 148:1]; and the other: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous" [Ps. 32:1].*[^529]

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Cheesefare Sunday evening [Forgiveness Vespers]:*[^531]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *We do not recite psalmody [Kathisma]. On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 10: in the Octoechos 4 Penitential of the incoming tone, and 3 in the Triodion, and to the Saint 3 in the Menaion; Glory, both now, Theotokion. At the Entrance: "O Gladsome Light." Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8: "Turn not away Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble; hear me speedily; attend unto my soul, and deliver it" [Ps. 68:18–19]; Verse: "Thy salvation, O God, hath upheld me" [Ps. 68:30]... ...Verse: "Let the poor see it, and be glad" [Ps. 68:33]. "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening [without sin]"; and 3 prostrations. Litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord." And both choirs having come together, they sing the daily Automela 2 and 4, in the same tone, once; Glory, both now, Theotokion. "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..."; and Trisagion; and 3 prostrations; after "Our Father...", [Priest:] "For Thine is the kingdom..."; Troparion: "Theotokos Virgin, rejoice..."; and one prostration; Glory: "O Baptist of Christ, remember us all..."; and a prostration; Both now: "Intercede for us, holy Apostles..."; and one prostration; "Beneath Thy compassion..."; without a prostration. "Lord, have mercy" 40 times; "O Heavenly King, strengthen our faithful kings..."; "Lord, have mercy" 3 times; Glory, both now; "More honorable than the Cherubim..."; "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Then the priest [says]: "He Who is blessed, Christ our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages"; and he makes 3 great prostrations with the prayer: "O Lord and Master of my life..."; and we kiss the holy icons, saying: "Forgive me wherein I have caused scandal, according to custom." The priest [says]: "Glory to Thee, Christ our God, our hope, glory to Thee!"; and a prayer from the priest, and the complete dismissal. This order ought to take place also on...*[^532]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: токмо · въ прочіа же дн҃и ст҃го поста · поетъ сѧ павечерница великаа · ѿ вънегда възъва с поклоны · и спѣниемь · такоже и полꙋно щницꙋ · НАЧАЛО СТ҃ГО ВЕЛИКАГО · Д҃ · РЕДЕ
units.english_cohort_translation: ...and on the other Sundays of the holy Great Fast. Compline is chanted small, from *Have mercy on me, O God* [Ps. 50], according to custom, on account of the labor of the All-Night Vigil. In this manner is Compline chanted on Cheesefare Sunday only. But on the remaining days of the holy Fast, Great Compline is chanted, from *When I called* [Ps. 4], with prostrations and with singing; likewise also the Midnight Office.

On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 10: in the Octoechos 4 Penitential of the incoming tone, and 3 in the Triodion, and to the Saint 3 in the Menaion; Glory, both now, Theotokion. At the Entrance: "O Gladsome Light." Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8: "Turn not away Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble; hear me speedily; attend unto my soul, and deliver it" [Ps. 68:18–19]; Verse: "Thy salvation, O God, hath upheld me" [Ps. 68:30]... ...Verse: "Let the poor see it, and be glad" [Ps. 68:33]. "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening [without sin]"; and 3 prostrations. Litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord." And both choirs having come together, they sing the daily Automela 2 and 4, in the same tone, once; Glory, both now, Theotokion. "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..."; and Trisagion; and 3 prostrations; after "Our Father...", [Priest:] "For Thine is the kingdom..."; Troparion: "Theotokos Virgin, rejoice..."; and one prostration; Glory: "O Baptist of Christ, remember us all..."; and a prostration; Both now: "Intercede for us, holy Apostles..."; and one prostration; "Beneath Thy compassion..."; without a prostration. "Lord, have mercy" 40 times; "O Heavenly King, strengthen our faithful kings..."; "Lord, have mercy" 3 times; Glory, both now; "More honorable than the Cherubim..."; "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Then the priest [says]: "He Who is blessed, Christ our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages"; and he makes 3 great prostrations with the prayer: "O Lord and Master of my life..."; and we kiss the holy icons, saying: "Forgive me wherein I have caused scandal, according to custom." The priest [says]: "Glory to Thee, Christ our God, our hope, glory to Thee!"; and a prayer from the priest, and the complete dismissal. This order ought to take place also on...

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Подобаеть вѣдати · ꙗко не приꙗхѡ стварѧ ти преждесщ҃еныꙗ до среды · понеже по пре данію ст҃ы ѡц҃ъ постатѧсѧ браꙗ всѧ до сре ды · могоущіи же до пѧтка · Егда же бꙋ деть преждесщ҃енаꙗ · Бываеть вечернѧ си це · по бл҃ви дꙋше моꙗ г҃а · сл҃а і н҃ а҃ллꙋа г҃ ·
units.english_cohort_translation: *Whenever there is the Presanctified [Liturgy], Vespers takes place as follows: After "Bless the Lord, O my soul" [Ps. 103], Glory, both now, "Alleluia" thrice, and 3 prostrations; the Great Litany, and the exclamation. And we recite the psalmody: "In my distress I cried unto the Lord" [Ps. 119; Kathisma 18]; Glory, both now, thrice, and 3 prostrations after each; and the priest says the Little Litany. After the psalmody we sing "Lord, I have cried" in the tone [of the week]; the troparia are in the Triodion; and we appoint 10 stichera, from "Bring my soul out of prison" [Ps. 141:8]: the Idiomelon of the day twice, and the Martyrikon in the same tone once; 3 Prosomoia in the Triodion, and of the Saint 3; and in the Menaion on 4, and the other twice; Glory, both now, Theotokion. Entrance with candles and with the censer, without the Gospel; "O Gladsome Light." Prokeimenon before the Old Testament reading, and Genesis is read. Another Prokeimenon; and the deacon exclaims: "Command!" (*κελεύσατε*)... ...Command!" (*κελεύσατε*).[^536] And the priest, having taken the censer and the candle in his right hand, stands before the Holy Table; and the deacon exclaims: "Wisdom! Let us attend!" And the priest, making the sign of the cross with the censer and with the candle, says: "The Light of Christ illumines all." Then the reader says: "The reading from Proverbs"; and the Proverbs of Solomon are read. The candle-lighter [kandilaptes] strikes the iron semantron [klepalo].[^537] And after the completion of the reading, the priest says: "Peace be unto thee"; and the singer begins: "Let my prayer be set forth [as incense before Thee]"; Verses: "Lord, I have cried unto Thee"; "Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth"; "Incline not my heart [to evil words]" [Ps. 140:1–4]. And it takes place as follows: When the singer sings "Let my prayer be set forth," then we fall prostrate on our faces. But when we, having arisen, sing "Let my prayer be set forth," then the singer himself falls prostrate on his face. After this, the deacon [says] the litany: "Let us all say unto the Lord..."; and we make 3 prostrations. And the rest of the order of the Presanctified takes place. And after the Entrance...*

Then we chant Vespers: "Bless the Lord, O my soul" [Ps. 103]; Glory, both now; "Alleluia" thrice, and 3 prostrations. We recite the psalmody: "In my distress I cried unto the Lord" [Ps. 119; Kathisma 18]. On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6: 3 in the Triodion, and of the Saint 3 in the Menaion; Glory, both now, Theotokion; "O Gladsome Light." Prokeimenon before the Old Testament reading, and Genesis is read, the first reading. Another Prokeimenon, and the Proverbs of Solomon are read. Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord," and prostrations... ...3 prostrations. And both choirs having come together, they chant the daily Automela 2 and 4, in the same tone, once; Glory, both now, Theotokion. "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..."; Trisagion; and 3 prostrations; Priest: "For Thine is the kingdom..."; Troparion: "Theotokos Virgin, rejoice..."; Glory: "O Baptist of Christ..."; Both now: "Intercede for us..."; and after each troparion, one prostration; then: "Beneath Thy compassion...", without a prostration. "Lord, have mercy" 40 times, quietly and evenly. The priest exclaims: "O God, be merciful unto us..."; and we make 3 great prostrations with the prayer: "O Lord and Master of my life..."; and the remaining 12 metanias; and at the last prostration, that entire prayer: "O Lord and Master of my life." Trisagion; and 3 prostrations; after "Our Father...", "Lord, have mercy" 12 times; "Blessed be the name of the Lord" thrice; and 3 prostrations; Glory, both now; "I will bless the Lord [at all times]"; and the dismissal. After this, we go out into the narthex, singing according to custom the sticheron of the Saint. And the priest says the customary prayers and the departure [litany], and the priest commemorates [the departed] with all the brethren; and there is the complete dismissal. This order of Vespers takes place in...

units.english_cohort_translation: *...with the Holy Gifts, at the conclusion of the chant "Now the powers of heaven [invisibly serve with us]," we make 3 prostrations, standing uncovered. And the priest takes both veils [sudaria] from the Holy Gifts according to custom, and covers both, that is, the diskos and the chalice, as with one, or with the aer.*[^538] *And when he wishes to elevate the Holy Lamb [artos],*[^539] *he takes the holy elevation, and the deacon says: "Let us attend!" And the priest, elevating the Holy Lamb, says: "The Presanctified Holy Things unto the holy!" Communion Hymn: "O taste and see that the Lord is good" [Ps. 33:9]; another: "I will bless the Lord [at all times]" [Ps. 33:1]. And they receive communion, and partake of the warm water ablution.*[^540] *After this: "Let our mouths be filled with Thy praise, O Lord..."; and three prostrations; and the Prayer behind the Ambon; then: "Blessed be the name of the Lord" now and unto ages of ages; and there is the complete dismissal. And after the dismissal, we enter the refectory; and this takes place on Wednesday, and we eat dry food [xerophagy]. But on Thursday a meal is not set, and we fast from Wednesday until Friday. On Friday we enter the refectory, and we eat dry food... ...dry food. And Great Compline we chant with prostrations and with singing, from "When I called" [Ps. 4].*

units.english_cohort_translation: *On Friday of the First Week of the Fast: At Vespers prostrations are omitted.*[^542] *We chant: "In my distress I cried unto the Lord" [Ps. 119; Kathisma 18]. Stichera on 10: the Idiomelon twice, and 4 of the Martyrs in the Octoechos of the current tone, and of Saint Theodore 3 on 4. Entrance without the Gospel; "O Gladsome Light." Prokeimenon and readings in the Old Testament lections. "Let my prayer be set forth," and 3 prostrations. Likewise also at "Now the powers of heaven" and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord," 3 great prostrations each; and the rest of the Presanctified service.*[^543]

In the fountain of flame, as upon the water of rest, the holy Martyr Theodore rejoiced; for having been consumed by fire, as sweet bread he was offered unto the Trinity. Communion Hymn: "In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be" [Ps. 111:6].*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Въ памѧть в · На трапезѣ же ꙗды ѡварꙋ ѡбвареноу · с маслинами бѣлы и черны ми · и масло и вареніе прилоучившеесѧ · и коли воу · и вина же пьемь по красоволю · ꙗко въ ст҃жа · м҃ · в҃ · приꙗхѡ ꙗсти рыбы · в пра здникы бл҃говѣщеніа · и в н҃елю цвѣтнꙋю ·

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Далъ еси достоꙗніе боꙗщимсѧ имени тво его · ст҃ · ѿ конецъ землѧ · сти · покрыюсѧ кровѡ крилоу твоею · ст҃ · тако въспою име ни твоємꙋ · та сподоби гн҃и · сїа же два ве ликаа прокымена · пѣрвыи · в н҃елю сырь нꙋю · вторыи же сеіи · иже премѣнаа · въ н҃елю жь · верь ст҃го сего поста · ѿ н҃ели · сы рныꙗ · до н҃ели · е҃ · по · ꙗко в началѣ · паве черници · в н҃елю вечерь · поклонь не твори тъ чьто по слава въ кышьни · и въ конець · єі ·
units.english_cohort_translation: *Exapostilarion, Resurrectional, and in the Triodion. On the Praises, on 8: Resurrectional 3, and in the Triodion on 4; then 3: "Arise, O Lord my God" [Ps. 9:33]; Idiomelon, Tone 6: "Moses in the season of abstinence..."; Glory, the same; Both now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."; and the Great Doxology. At the Liturgy: the Octoechos on 6, and in the Triodion, Ode 3. Prokeimenon: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers" [Dan. 3:26]; Verse: "For Thou art righteous in all that Thou hast done" [Dan. 3:27]. Epistle: "By faith Moses, when he was come to years..." [Heb. 11:24–26, 32–12:2]. Alleluia: "Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among them that call upon His name" [Ps. 98:6]. Gospel from John [1:43–51]: "The day following Jesus would go forth..." Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens" [Ps. 148:1]; and the other: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous" [Ps. 32:1].*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Cheesefare Sunday evening [Forgiveness Vespers]:*[^531]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On the evening of that same Sunday: as on Cheesefare Sunday. Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8: "Thou hast given an heritage unto them that fear Thy name, O Lord" [Ps. 60:6]; Verse: "From the ends of the earth have I cried unto Thee" [Ps. 60:3]; Verse: "I will be sheltered under the shadow of Thy wings" [Ps. 60:5]; Verse: "So will I sing praise unto Thy name unto ages of ages" [Ps. 60:9]. Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." Now these two Great Prokeimena: the first on Cheesefare... ...Sunday, and the second this one, which alternate on the Sunday evenings of this holy Fast, from Cheesefare Sunday until the 5th Sunday. After [Vespers], as at the beginning, at Compline on Sunday evening prostrations are not made, except only after "Glory to God in the highest," and at the end 15 [metanias] and the last [great prostration]; after the Trisagion, 3.*[^554]

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Cheesefare Sunday evening [Forgiveness Vespers]:*[^531]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *And on Saturday [Memorial Saturday] at Matins: "Alleluia." Troparion: "Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs..."; Glory: "Remember, O Lord, Thy servants..."; Both now: "Holy Mother of the ineffable Light..." After the 1st Kathisma: 4 Sessional hymns, both funeral and Theotokion. "Blessed are the undefiled" [Ps. 118; Kathisma 17], which is divided in two: in the middle, the diaconal litany for the reposed; and at the end, three Sessional hymns, and the diaconal litany for the reposed; and the priest commemorates all the reposed; and the rest [of the service]. Canon in the Menaion with the heirmos on 6, and of the temple on 4; is chanted in order... ...Troparia without verses, and keep 3. From then on take care that one does not recite the stichologia from the start of the canticles until Ode 6. At Ode 6, where the Four-Ode Canon enters, then one recites the stichologia: Ode 6, likewise also Ode 7, and the rest.*[^557] *Exapostilarion: "O Thou Who hast adorned the heaven with stars"; and for the departed, the sessional hymn. On the Praises, daily stichera; Glory: for the reposed; on the Aposticha, Sessional hymns for the reposed. At the Liturgy: Beatitudes in the Octoechos; Prokeimenon, Epistle of the day, and for the reposed; and the Gospel likewise: of the day, and for the reposed of the day, and for the dead. In this manner the service takes place on all Saturdays until the 4th Saturday of the Fast, except for three feasts.*

Canon in the Menaion with the heirmos on 6, and of the temple on 4; is chanted in order... ...Troparia without verses, and keep 3. From then on take care that one does not recite the stichologia from the start of the canticles until Ode 6. At Ode 6, where the Four-Ode Canon enters, then one recites the stichologia: Ode 6, likewise also Ode 7, and the rest.*[^557] *Exapostilarion: "O Thou Who hast adorned the heaven with stars"; and for the departed, the sessional hymn. On the Praises, daily stichera; Glory: for the reposed; on the Aposticha, Sessional hymns for the reposed. At the Liturgy: Beatitudes in the Octoechos; Prokeimenon, Epistle of the day, and for the reposed; and the Gospel likewise: of the day, and for the reposed of the day, and for the dead. In this manner the service takes place on all Saturdays until the 4th Saturday of the Fast, except for three feasts.*

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *The Third Sunday of the Fast, on which we celebrate the Veneration of the Precious Cross: At Great Vespers... ...Stichera on 10: Resurrectional 6, and of the Cross on 4; the tone of the Cross: Automelon 1. At the Entrance: Theotokion Dogmatikon of the tone; Glory, Tone 5: "Beholding Thee, O Christ, hanging upon the Tree..."; on the Aposticha: Resurrectional; Glory, Tone 4: "O Lord Who didst help gentle David..."; Both now, the same. Troparion: "Theotokos Virgin, rejoice..." twice; Tone 1: "Save, O Lord, Thy people..." once; this makes 3. At Matins: Troparion, Resurrectional twice; Glory, both now, of the Cross; and the rest the customary order. Canons: Resurrectional on 4, and of the Theotokos on 2, and of the Cross on 8; Katavasia: "Divine Moses prefigured of old...". After Ode 3, Sessional hymn of the Cross. After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 7, Automelon:*[^559]

units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of the Precious Cross [Tone 7]:* No longer doth the flaming sword guard the gate of Eden, for upon it hath come a marvelous bond, the Tree of the Cross! The sting of death and the victory of Hades have been destroyed, for Thou didst appear, O my Savior, crying unto those in faith: Enter ye again into Paradise!

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ст̑ры . на ҃і . въскр̑ны ҃ѕ . и кр҃тоу . на ҃д . гл҃а кр҃тоу . ҃і н б҃о . ҃а . на исхо . бц҃и . сла̂ гл҃а ҃е . видаще тѧ . на стї . въскресень . сла̂ гл҃а ҃д . пособнвыи гн҃и . ҃і н того . тр҃о бц҃е дв҃ко ҃в . гл҃а ҃а . спси гн҃и люди своꙗ . ҃а . се ҃г . на у̂ тр҃о . въскрпнь . ҃в . сл̑а ҃і н кр҃тꋋ и прочее . ѡбычно . ка въскресень . на ҃д . и бц҃и на ҃в . и кр҃тоу . на ҃и . катава . бж҃ествьныи проѡбрази . по ҃г . пѣ сѣ кр҃тꋋ по ҃ѕ . кѡ҃ . гл҃а ҃з . самогл̑ны . Оуже пламенное ѡрꋋжїе не хранить врать едемскы . прїиде бо емоу преславныи игл̑а . древо кр҃стьное . смертное жало . и адова побѣда погоублена бы . приде бо сп҃съ мои , въпїа въ рныи . вънидете пакы въ раи:~ свѣ . въскресень . и кр҃тоу . на хва . постави . на ҃и . ҃д . въскрны . и кр҃тоу . по̂ гл҃а ҃д . на ҃д . ҃в . по̂ . кр҃тоу . поютсѧ . съ стї . ҃г . б҃ъ же цр҃ь наш̑ь . с҃ . кланꙗитесѧ по̂но̂ . по се . гл̑етсѧ .
units.english_cohort_translation: *Exapostilarion: Resurrectional, and of the Cross. On the Praises, appoint 8: 4 Resurrectional; and of the Cross, Prosomoia in Tone 4, on 4: 2 Prosomoia of the Cross are chanted with the 3 verses: "God is our King before the ages..." [Ps. 73:12]; Verse: "Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool..." [Ps. 98:5]. After this is said... ...another Resurrectional verse and the Prosomoia; and one sings the Idiomelon of the day in that tone, Tone 8: "The boast of the faithful..."; Glory, Tone 6: "Today the Cross of the Lord..."; Both now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."; Great Doxology, sung in a quiet voice. After this Doxology, the priest vests in the phelonion, and comes with the censer and with a candle unto the Holy Table, and censes the Holy Table and the Precious Wood; and thus he lifts it upon his head, in his hands, upon a platter. And he goes by the left side of the altar, two great candles and the censer preceding him. He comes unto the church doors, and there stands awaiting the end of the Trisagion.*[^560] *And when the Trisagion is finished, the deacon says: "Wisdom! Let us attend!" And the brethren begin the Troparion: "Save, O Lord, Thy people...", chanting it thrice. And the priest comes, carrying the Precious Wood through the Holy Doors unto the prepared table, and places the Precious Wood upon the table. And thus...*

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *...thus he censes it on the 4 sides. And while they sing: "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship, O Master, and Thy holy Resurrection we glorify", immediately uncovering the casket, they begin to make prostrations in this manner: The Igumen with the priest make 3 prostrations unto the ground, and kiss the Precious Cross; and having kissed it, they again make 1 prostration, both together, and step back to their places. In like manner also the brethren begin, two from the right side and from the left side, after the same manner.*[^561] *And the choirs sing the Idiomelon Stichera: Tone 2: "Come, ye faithful, let us worship the life-giving Wood...", and the others which belong to the Cross; Glory, both now, Tone 8: "Today the Master of creation and Lord of glory is nailed to the Cross..." And when the kissing is completed, then the litany and dismissal. At the Liturgy: Beatitudes in the Octoechos on 6, and of the Cross, Ode 3; Troparion: Resurrectional, and of the Cross; Glory, both now, Kontakion of the Cross. In place of the Trisagion: "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship..." Prokeimenon: "Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance" [Ps. 27:9]; Verse: "Unto Thee will I cry, O Lord my God" [Ps. 27:1]. Epistle of the day [Heb. 4:14–5:6]. Alleluia: "Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning" [Ps. 73:2]; Verse: "God is our King before the ages, Who hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth" [Ps. 73:12]. Gospel of the day [Mark 8:34–9:1]. Communion Hymn: "The light of Thy countenance is signed upon us, O Lord" [Ps. 4:7].*

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *Be it known that this veneration we perform according to the aforesaid manner for 4 days, that is: on Sunday, on Monday, on Wednesday, and on Friday.*[^562] *And it takes place as follows: On Monday, at the First Hour one makes the veneration, while chanting instead of the dismissal troparion: "Before Thy Cross we bow down in worship...". In like manner also on Wednesday, after the same manner. But on Friday, at the Sixth Hour, we perform the third veneration, and venerate the Cross, and thus the Cross is taken up into the sanctuary. On Saturday evening of the 4th week: the customary stichologia, and the rest according to custom. On Wednesday of the 4th week, at Matins is chanted the Canon of the Cross with the Triodia; of the Saint it is left out. In that same 4th week, the priest begins the twofold litanies of the catechumens: "As many as are catechumens, depart...", with the prayer, even until Great Wednesday.*[^563] *On the 4th Sunday of the Fast, at Vespers: one recites the stichologia: Kathisma 4; and on Monday of the 5th week: one recites the stichologia: the Kathismata in order. In the evening, on Wednesday of the 5th week: at Vespers, the customary stichologia, and on "Lord, I have cried," Idiomela... ...Idiomela of the day: 2, and 4; and after 3 stichera, in the Triodion; and immediately we sing the 24 Stichera of the Great Canon, whose acrostic is: "Falling into the nets...". And at each sticheron we make 3 prostrations. Then Glory, Triadikon; Both now, Theotokion from the same; and the rest of the order of the Presanctified. In the refectory, we eat food with oil from tree-fruit, and we drink wine, on account of the labor of the All-Night Vigil. And Compline we chant in the cells. On Thursday of the 5th week, at Matins we sing "Alleluia," and in the current tone is said the Hymn to the Trinity. And one recites the stichologia: one Kathisma, 7 in the Octoechos, and of the Apostles 4; and we read from the book of Saint Ephrem; and Psalm 50. And we begin the Great Canon of master Andrew; and at each troparion we make 3 prostrations. And there is read the Life of Saint Mary of Egypt, in two readings: after Ode 3 in the Triodion; at Ode 4 the Triodion precedes, without prostrations; likewise also at Ode 8 and at Ode 9.*[^564]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: по ҃ѕ . ко̂ . гл҃а ҃ѕ . по̂ . иже ѡ спа̂ . Дꋋше моꙗ дꋋше моꙗ въстани что спиши , конець приближаетсѧ и долвитї имаши . воспрѧни оу̂бо да пощадить тѧ хс҃ б҃ъ , йже вездѣ сыи , и всꙗ исплънаꙗ:~ та̂ ҃і ко̂ . и а҃бїе . бл҃жена . и покло̂ . та̂ и пѣ ҃з . и прѡа . свѣ . въ ѡ . на стї . самогл̑ны . д̑невн . ҃в . и д̑і . сла̂ ҃і ко̂ . и а҃ . та̂ . без стїхословна . та̂ . ка̂ . по̂е . на верни . въ ъпѧ е҃ . нѣ . вечерь . ст̑ры на ҃і . самогл̑ны . д̑невн , ҃в . и дїж . и ст҃ыꙗ бца . по̂ ҃г . гл҃а ҃ѕ . на ҃з . свѣтъ превѣчныи . сла̂ ҃і н҃ гл҃а ҃в . ѡ вѣка таиньство . и прочее . слꋋ̂ба . преждесщ҃еннаꙗ . на верницꙗ . ма̂а . вежботу нау̂рн . тр҃о . ҃г . гл҃а ҃и . Повелѣнное таинъство прие̂мь въ разꋋмѣ . въ кровѣ їѡсифовѣ , скоро преста бесплътныи , гл̑а неискоусобрачьнѣи . преклонивыи нисхоженїе̂мь нб҃са . въмѣщаетсѧ неизмѣнновъвъта . егоже и ви дѧ въ ложеснѣ твои прїимша рабїи зракъ . оу̂жасаюсѧ зватити , радоуисѧ невѣсто неневѣстнаꙗ:~ ка̂ ҃з . двѣ . по ҃а . ка̂ ҃з . ко̂ гл҃а ҃и . въꙁбраннои . та̂ ико̂ . ҃ѕ . ѵпакои . ко̂ т҃о . е̂гда же , гл̑ютьсїа икоси . ц҃ы не сѣди , тогда . ностоꙗще слоушае̂мь съ страхо̂ . по ҃в . ка̂ . ко̂ . въꙁбраннои ко . и прочїі икосы ҃ѕ . и пакы кѡ҃ . то̂ . ѱло̂ . н҃ . кано̂ бц҃и не сѣдающаго . гл҃ ҃д . на ҃и . а прехрамоу на ҃ѕ . и йдеже . четверопѣц ино храмо̂ ѡложи . и бц҃и на ҃ѕ . по ҃г . пѣ кѡ҃ . въꙁбраннои . и икѡвь . ҃ѕ . и пакы тотъжь ко̂ . по ҃ѕ . пѣ четверопѣтна . по ѡбычаю . по ҃ѕ . пѣ кѡ҃ . въꙁбраннои . и икѡвь ҃ѕ . и пакы кѡ то̂ . и ико̂сь ҃а . по ҃ѳ . свѣ бц҃и . на хва . по̂бникы ьц҃и на ҃д . слава и ннѣ . ꙗзыка егоже . славословье . трори бц҃и . на лѵтоургїе . бл҃женна . ѡканона . бц҃и пѣ ҃г . и ҃ѕ . про велїчи дше моꙗ га̂
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion of the Akathist [Tone 8]:* When the bodiless angel perceived the mystic command, he came with haste unto the abode of Joseph, and said unto her that knew not wedlock: He that bowed the heavens by His descent is held without change wholly within Thee; Whom also beholding Whom also beholding in Thy womb taking the form of a servant, in awe I cry unto Thee: Rejoice, O Bride unwedded!

units.english_cohort_translation: *Kathisma psalmody: two Kathismata. After the 1st Kathisma, Kontakion, Tone 8: "To thee, the Champion Leader..."; then 6 Ikoses; Hypakoe; the same Kontakion. And when these Ikoses are said, one does not sit down, but standing we listen with fear.*[^566] *After the 2nd Kathisma: Kontakion: "To thee, the Champion Leader...", and the remaining 6 Ikoses, and again that same Kontakion. Psalm 50. Canon of the Theotokos, of the Akathist [non-sitting], Tone 4, on 8; and for the patron Saint of the church on 6; and where the Four-Ode Canon occurs, omit that of the church, and for the Theotokos on 6. After Ode 3, Kontakion: "To thee, the Champion Leader...", and 6 Ikoses, and again that same Kontakion. After Ode 6, the Four-Ode Canon according to custom. After Ode 6, Kontakion: "To thee, the Champion Leader...", and 6 Ikoses, and again that same Kontakion, and Ikos 1. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the Theotokos. On the Praises: Prosomoia of the Theotokos on 4; Glory, both now: "A language which she knew not..." [Tone 2]. Great Doxology; Troparion of the Theotokos. At the Liturgy: Beatitudes from the Canon of the Theotokos, Ode 3 and Ode 6. Prokeimenon: "My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Savior" [Luke 1:46–47]... ...Verse: "For He hath regarded the lowliness of His handmaiden" [Luke 1:48]. Epistle: [Hebrews], pericope 320 [Heb. 9:1–7]: "For both He that sanctifies and they who are sanctified are all of one..." Alleluia: "Unto Thy face shall the rich among the people make supplication" [Ps. 44:13]. Gospel: [Luke], pericope 54 [Luke 1:39–49, 56]: "In those days, Mary arose..." Communion Hymn: "I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord" [Ps. 115:4].*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: В сꋋботоу , ст҃го лазарꙗ , на оу̂трни . тр҃о . гл҃а ҃а . ҃г . на б҃ъ гь , О̂бщее , въскресенїе прежде своеꙗ стр҃ти извѣщавь . йз мр҃твы , въскрѣсилъ е̂си лазарѧ хс҃е б҃же . тѣмь и мы ꙗко ѡтроци побѣдныꙗ ѡбразы , приносѧще , побѣдителю смр҃ти възъпїемь , ѡсанна въ вышнихъ , блгвнъ грѧдыи въ ймѧ гн҃е:~ по ҃в . ка̂ . по бл҃женни непорочни . тр҃ори . въскр̑ныи , а̂ггльскыи съборъ . и гледъ . въскресенїе хв҃о . ѱло̂ н҃ . кано̂ гл҃ ҃а . пѣнь побѣдноую . съерм̑ль . на ҃и . и инь . гл҃а ҃и . безъерм̑ло . на ҃ѕ . по ҃г . пѣсѣ празнй . по ҃ѕ . пѣ кѡ҃ . гл҃а , ҃в . Всѣхъ радос хс҃ истина свѣтъ и животъ . на мироу въздвиженїе . сꋋщимь на земли ꙗви сѧ своею блгтїю . въскресенїꙗ ѡбразъ бывь . и всѣмь подаꙗ въскрсенїе:~ свѣ . въ триѡ . на хва . самогл̑ны , ҃д . гл҃а ҃а . въскресенїе и жизнь . и два гл҃ д҃ . марѳа
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion of Lazarus Saturday [Tone 1]:* Giving assurance of the universal resurrection before Thy Passion, Thou didst raise Lazarus from the dead, O Christ God. Therefore, we also, like the children, bearing the emblems of victory, cry out unto Thee, the Vanquisher of death: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord!

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Saturday of Saint Lazarus [Lazarus Saturday], at Matins: Troparion, Tone 1, thrice, at "God is the Lord":*[^568]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *...Mary [said]: "Lord, he that hath been four days dead stinks already" [John 11:39]. After this, coming together, both choirs sing two by two; Sticheron, Tone 8: "Beholding Lazarus dead, as Thou didst say, O Lord..."; Verse: that same verse: "Arise, O Lord my God, let Thine hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor for ever" [Ps. 9:33]; Glory, Tone 2: "Great and marvelous wonders hath the Savior wrought..."; Both now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."; Great Doxology; Troparion, and dismissal. At the Liturgy: Beatitudes from the Canon, Ode 3 and Ode 6, on 8. In place of the Trisagion: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia" [Gal. 3:27].*[^569] *Prokeimenon: "The Lord is my light and my Savior; whom shall I fear?" [Ps. 26:1]; Verse: "The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?" [Ps. 26:1]. Epistle of the day: [Hebrews, pericope 333; Heb. 12:28–13:8]. Alleluia, Tone 5: "The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty" [Ps. 92:1]; Verse: "For He hath established the world, which shall not be shaken" [Ps. 92:1]. Gospel according to John, of the day [John 11:1–45]. Communion Hymn: "Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast Thou perfected praise [Ps. 8:3]. Alleluia."*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ше̃стый д̃нь• с̃л д̃нь блг̃ть• і н̃ того• въхо̃ про̃• Г̃ь въц̃рися• ч̃тем г̃• праз̃• на исхо̃ самогла̃ны г̃• гла̃ а̃• всестыи, съвез̃налныи• пре̃шести д̃ни• и ина• два• гла̃ в̃• въходящю ти• с̃л того• сла̃ і н̃ г̃• пре̃шести д̃ни• на сти̃• самогла̃ны• гла̃ и̃• рау̃ися• и ина и два• с̃ тиже г̃ле• изъ оусть младенець• с̃• г̃и б̃е мои• сла̃ д̃нь блг̃ть• і н̃ пакы того• по тр̃то• тр̃о• в̃• Общее въскр̃сеніе• и нь• гла̃ д̃• единою• съпогребшотнеся кр̃щеніемь х̃е б̃е нашъ• бессмрътнаго живота сподобихомся въскр̃сеніемь твоимь• тѣмь въспѣвающе зовемь• блг̃внъ грядыи въ имя г̃не:~ на оу̃• на б̃ъ г̃ь• тро̃ Общее въскр̃сеніе• в̃• сла̃ і н̃ с погребшюти• с̃тие лови д̃вѣ ка̃• и многомл̃остивы• с̃ѣ праз̃ с те г̃ д̃• а̃нти а̃• про г̃ д̃• изъ оусть мла̃• с̃• г̃и б̃е мои• еѵ̃е ѿ ма̃• егда приближис̃• ѱ̃ло н̃• в̃оскр̃ніе х̃во не г̃лаетс̃я•

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Saturday of Saint Lazarus [Lazarus Saturday], at Matins: Troparion, Tone 1, thrice, at "God is the Lord":*[^568]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *At Matins: at "God is the Lord," Troparion: "Giving assurance of the universal resurrection..." twice; Glory, both now: "Buried with Thee in baptism..." Stichologia: two Kathismata, and the Polyeleos [Many-merciful, Pss. 134–135]. Sessional hymn of the feast; Anabathmoi [Hymns of Ascent], Tone 4, Antiphon 1 ["From my youth..."]. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast Thou perfected praise" [Ps. 8:3]; Verse: "O Lord our Lord, how marvelous is Thy name in all the earth!" [Ps. 8:2, 10]. Gospel according to Matthew [Matt. 21:1–17]: "When Jesus drew near unto Jerusalem..." Psalm 50; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" is not said.*[^572]

Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast Thou perfected praise" [Ps. 8:3]; Verse: "O Lord our Lord, how marvelous is Thy name in all the earth!" [Ps. 8:2, 10]. Gospel according to Matthew [Matt. 21:1–17]: "When Jesus drew near unto Jerusalem..." Psalm 50; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" is not said.*[^572]

units.slavonic_incipit: Егдаже братия цѣлують• еѵ̃ліе• раздаваеть игоуменъ•
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: егдаже братия целуют еилие раздавает игоумен ваия еже
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Егдаже братия цѣлують• еѵ̃ліе• раздаваеть игоуменъ• ваия• еже бѣтви• и начинаемь кано̃• гла̃ д̃• [я]вишася исто• ір̃мъ• по в̃• и тр̃ори• на, в̃і• и пакы• ір̃мъ• а̃• в коу̃• по ѕ̃• пѣ к̃о̃ гла̃ ѕ̃• На прѣстолѣ на нб̃си на жребяти на земли, сѣдяи х̃е б̃е• ѿ а̃г̃глъ хваленіе, и ѿ ѡ̃трокъ пѣніе пріймяше• въпіющих, блг̃венъ грядыи а̃дама възъдвигноути:~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of Palm Sunday [Tone 6]:* Borne upon a throne in heaven, and upon a foal on earth, O Christ God, Thou didst accept the praise of angels and the singing of children, who cried out: Blessed art Thou that comest to raise up Adam!
units.slavonic_text: Егдаже братия цѣлують• еѵ̃ліе• раздаваеть игоуменъ• ваия• еже бѣтви• и начинаемь кано̃• гла̃ д̃• [я]вишася исто• ір̃мъ• по в̃• и тр̃ори• на, в̃і• и пакы• ір̃мъ• а̃• в коу̃• по ѕ̃• пѣ к̃о̃ гла̃ ѕ̃• На прѣстолѣ на нб̃си на жребяти на земли, сѣдяи х̃е б̃е• ѿ а̃г̃глъ хваленіе, и ѿ ѡ̃трокъ пѣніе пріймяше• въпіющих, блг̃венъ грядыи а̃дама възъдвигноути:~

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Егдаже братия цѣлують• еѵ̃ліе• раздаваеть игоуменъ• ваия• еже бѣтви• и начинаемь кано̃• гла̃ д̃• [я]вишася исто• ір̃мъ• по в̃• и тр̃ори• на, в̃і• и пакы• ір̃мъ• а̃• в коу̃• по ѕ̃• пѣ к̃о̃ гла̃ ѕ̃• На прѣстолѣ на нб̃си на жребяти на земли, сѣдяи х̃е б̃е• ѿ а̃г̃глъ хваленіе, и ѿ ѡ̃трокъ пѣніе пріймяше• въпіющих, блг̃венъ грядыи а̃дама възъдвигноути:~ Даются свѣщи н̃браи• с̃вѣ• г̃• на хва̃• ст̃ры• на ѕ̃• самогла̃нь• д̃• гла̃ д̃• и множество хотящоу• и зижитель• ѡ̃бщее въскр̃ніе• сла̃ і н̃ ѕ̃• преже шестии д̃ни• славословіе• тр̃о и ѡ̃поу̃• Въ, в̃• ча̃ д̃ни• [зри] ѡ̃биходимь• съ кр̃ты• манастырь• и възвращьшеся• начинаемь• а̃• ча̃:~ и сътворяемь• літоургію ранее троуда ради:~ на літоургіи• а̃нтины• а̃нти̃• а̃• ѱаломь• Възлюбихъ [я]ко оуслыша г̃ь гласъ моленіа моегое• мл̃твами б̃ца• с̃•

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Saturday of Saint Lazarus [Lazarus Saturday], at Matins: Troparion, Tone 1, thrice, at "God is the Lord":*[^568]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *Candles are given unto the brethren; Exapostilarion thrice: ["Holy is the Lord our God"]. On the Praises: Stichera on 6: Idiomela 4, Tone 4: "And a great multitude...", "He that desired...", "The Creator...", "Giving assurance of the universal resurrection..."; Glory, both now, Tone 6: "Six days before the Passover..." Great Doxology, Troparion, and dismissal. Note: At the second hour of the day, we process with crosses around the monastery, and having returned, we begin the First Hour; and we celebrate the Liturgy earlier, on account of the labor.*[^574] *At the Liturgy: Festal Antiphons:*[^575] *Antiphon 1, Psalm [114]: "I have loved, because the Lord hath heard the voice of my supplication" [Ps. 114:1]; Refrain: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us"; Verse: ..."I have loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my supplication; because He hath inclined His ear unto me" [Ps. 114:1–2]; Refrain: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos, Savior, save us"; Verse: "Therefore will I call upon Him in my days" [Ps. 114:2]; Refrain: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos..."; Verse: "The pangs of death encompassed me, the perils of Hades found me" [Ps. 114:3]; Refrain: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos, Savior, save us"; Glory: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos..."; Both now: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos..."*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Saturday of Saint Lazarus [Lazarus Saturday], at Matins: Troparion, Tone 1, thrice, at "God is the Lord":*[^568]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *Entrance: "Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us" [Ps. 117:26–27]. Troparion: "Giving assurance of the universal resurrection..."; Glory, both now: Kontakion: "Borne upon a throne in heaven..." Prokeimenon: "Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord" [Ps. 117:26]; Verse: "O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures unto the ages" [Ps. 117:1]. Epistle of the day: [Philippians, pericope 247; Phil. 4:4–9]: "Rejoice in the Lord alway..." Alleluia: "O sing unto the Lord a new song" [Ps. 97:1]; Verse: "All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God" [Ps. 97:3]. Gospel according to John, pericope [John 12:1–18]: "Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany..." And the rest of the Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Communion Hymn: "Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us [Ps. 117:26–27]. Alleluia." In the refectory there is consolation, a great meal: we eat fish and we drink wine.*[^577]

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Saturday of Saint Lazarus [Lazarus Saturday], at Matins: Troparion, Tone 1, thrice, at "God is the Lord":*[^568]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On that same Palm Sunday evening, at Vespers: we do not recite the Kathisma.*[^578] *Stichera on 6, Tone 8: "Rejoice and be glad, O city of Zion..."; Glory: again "Rejoice and be glad..."; Both now: "Borne upon the Cherubim..." Entrance; Great Prokeimenon: "Behold now, bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord" [Ps. 133:1]; Verse: "Who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God" [Ps. 133:1]; and 3 prostrations. On the Aposticha: Idiomela 3: one in Tone 2: "Bearing branches and boughs..."; another in Tone 3: "A dreadful... ...mystery"; another in Tone 6: "The assembly of the deceitful..."; we say the verses: "Sing unto the Lord a new song" [Ps. 97:1]; "All the ends of the earth have seen" [Ps. 97:3]; Glory: "Bearing branches and boughs..."; Both now: that same "A dreadful mystery..." After the Trisagion: "Theotokos Virgin, rejoice...", and the rest; the customary prostrations; dismissal.*

units.english_cohort_translation: *Note: Be it known that in this Great Week we complete the Psalter once, which is as follows:*[^579] *On Flowery Sunday [Palm Sunday]: 3 Kathismata at Compline [and Nocturns]. On Monday: 5 Kathismata, that is: at Matins 3, and at the Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours: 2. Likewise also on Great Tuesday: 5; and on Wednesday: 5, after the same manner. At Vespers, moreover, on those 3 days we chant: "In my distress I cried unto the Lord" [Ps. 119; Kathisma 18]; and "Blessed are the undefiled" [Ps. 118; Kathisma 17] we chant on Great Saturday at Matins.*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: и пакы• ір̃мь• а̃• въкоупѣ• поемь• пѣ̃ни к̃о̃• гла̃ и̃• [я]ко начаткы• [Я]кѡ вьрыдаяше• іѡсифова лишеніа• [я]ко въ колесницѣ сѣдяше• на колесници [я]ко оурьчтоль• егѵптанынне ѡ̃сласти тогда не поработивься славляяше• И нынѣ славится ѡ̃ всевидящаго ч̃лчьская ср̃д̃ца• и посылающаго вѣнець ненетлѣнныи:~ с̃вѣ гла̃ и̃• Чертога твоего г̃• поетжеся• посре̃ цр̃кви• и пакы ѡ̃бою страноу• на хва̃• самогла̃ны• г̃• на д̃• единь• гла̃ а̃• Приходя г̃ь• е̃ два• е̃го• Постигше• г̃и гряди• сла̃ і н̃ гла̃ и̃• Исухъшьша• на сти̃• самогла̃ны• г̃• гла̃ е̃• Г̃и к таинъ• г̃и съкръши• постигше его• с̃ти же г̃лемь• Въспоите г̃ви• с̃ти• Видѣша въси• сла̃ і н̃ гла̃ и̃• И съвкоупляемь• а̃• ча̃• без стихословья• по обычаю• г̃, [я]же ча̃ ѕ̃• с̃ стихословьемь• въ свое время:~ на часѣх же• г̃лется• к̃о̃ д̃невн• трори• ѡ̃бычныя• Подобаеть вѣдати• како, чести тетро• еѵ̃ліе• Иже ѿ ма̃а̃• еѵ̃ліе• чтется на два• ч̃теня все• тако̃• и ѿ марка• вьсе надвое• И еже ѿ лоу̃• чтется на г̃• ч̃теня• И еже ѡ̃ іѡ̃а• чтется• до начала ст̃ыя страстеи• на два• ч̃теня• Чтоут же еѵ̃ліа, въ три д̃ни• в п̃не• въ в̃то• въ ср̃е• на г̃• ѕ̃• и ѳ̃• мь часѣ• Въ ст̃ыи великыи, в п̃не• вечерь• с̃тры• на ѕ̃• Итыя оутрѣ• с̃л і н̃• гла̃ и̃• Второую еввоу• въхо̃• съ еѵ̃ліемь ч̃тене• парміи• Да ся исправить мл̃итва, т̃а еѵ̃ліе• ѿ ма̃а̃• Сѣдящю іс̃оу на горѣ• и екте̃я• Ръцѣмь вьси• и прое• слоужба• прежес̃щен̃ны• и въходимь въ трапезу• [я]мы соухояденіе• т̃аи до великаго, четвертка• павечерница же поется великаа по ѡ̃бычаю• на неи же тр̃ипѣсна г̃на а̃ндреа Въ в̃то• великыи• на оу̃р, пое• а̃ллилуа• въ гла̃ и̃• и г̃лемь• тр̃о• г̃• Се жени грядеть [Кустод: о̃б]
units.english_cohort_translation: *Exapostilarion, Tone 8: "Thy Bridal Chamber, O Lord, I behold adorned, and a garment I have not that I may enter therein; enlighten the vesture of my soul, O Giver of Light, and save me", chanted thrice in the midst of the church, and again by both sides [choirs].*[^582] *On the Praises: Idiomela 3, on 4: one in Tone 1: "The Lord, going unto His voluntary Passion..."; and the other two: "Having reached the saving Passion...", "Lord, coming unto Thy Passion..."; Glory, both now, Tone 8: "Finding the fig tree withered [because of its barrenness]..." On the Aposticha: Idiomela 3, Tone 5: "Lord, reaching the mystery...", "Lord, Thou hast crushed...", "Having reached..."; and we say the verses: "Sing unto the Lord a new song" [Ps. 97:1]; Verse: "All the ends of the earth have seen" [Ps. 97:3]; Glory, both now, Tone 8: ["A second Eve the serpent found in the Egyptian woman..."]. And we join the First Hour, without stichologia, according to custom; but the Third and Sixth Hours with stichologia at their proper time. At the Hours, moreover, there is said the Kontakion of the day, and the troparia... ...the customary ones. It is fitting to know how the Four Gospels [Tetraevangelion] are read:*[^583] *The Gospel of Matthew is read entirely in two readings; likewise also that of Mark, entirely in two; and that of Luke is read in three readings; and that of John is read up to the beginning of the Holy Passion in two readings. And they read the Gospels during the three days: on Monday, on Tuesday, and on Wednesday, at the Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours.*

And we join the First Hour, without stichologia, according to custom; but the Third and Sixth Hours with stichologia at their proper time. At the Hours, moreover, there is said the Kontakion of the day, and the troparia... ...the customary ones. It is fitting to know how the Four Gospels [Tetraevangelion] are read:*[^583] *The Gospel of Matthew is read entirely in two readings; likewise also that of Mark, entirely in two; and that of Luke is read in three readings; and that of John is read up to the beginning of the Holy Passion in two readings. And they read the Gospels during the three days: on Monday, on Tuesday, and on Wednesday, at the Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours.*

units.english_cohort_translation: *On Holy and Great Monday, at Vespers: Stichera on 6: "Going on the morrow unto His voluntary Passion..."; Glory, both now, Tone 8: "A second Eve the serpent found in the Egyptian woman..." Entrance with the Gospel; readings of the Paremias [Ex. 1:1–20; Job 1:1–12]; "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before Thee..."; then the Gospel according to Matthew [Matt. 24:3–35]: "As Jesus sat upon the Mount of Olives..."; and the litany: "Let us all say with our whole soul...", and the rest of the Presanctified Liturgy. And we enter into the refectory: we eat dry food [xerophagy], even until Great Thursday.*[^584] *Compline is chanted Great, according to custom, on which is chanted the Triodion of master Andrew.*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: по ка̃тѣ въ триѡ̃• ѱло̃ н̃• и мл̃• С̃п̃си б̃е люди• И начинае̃ триѡ̃• г̃ла козмы ір̃м• по в̃• а трорѣ• на в̃і• и пакы ір̃мь• едино̃• въкоу̃• По второи• пѣ̃ к̃о̃• гла̃ в̃• Часъ д̃ше конечныи помысливши• и посѣщеніа смоковница оубоявшися• данный ти талантъ троудолюбно дѣлаи ѡ̃каянная, бодръствоующи и зовоущи• да непревѣдемь вънѣ чертога х̃ва:~ с̃вѣ г̃• На хва̃• самогла̃ны в̃• по в̃• гла̃ а̃• Въ свѣтлостѣ гла̃ д̃• Съкрывша• сла̃ і н̃ гла̃ в̃• Д̃шевною• На сти̃• самогла̃ны• г̃• гла̃ ѕ̃• Придѣте вѣрніи• Женіі• Оучисти• сла̃ і н̃ ѕ̃• Егда придеши, с̃• г̃лемь• И спл̃ънихомся• И б̃жди свѣтло• и прое• ѡ̃быно• Въ в̃то, вечерь• С̃тры• е̃• на ѕ̃• Пѣтыя оутрѣ• сла̃ гла̃ з̃• Се тобѣ• і н̃ ѕ̃• Егда придеши• въхо̃• съ еѵ̃ліемь• ч̃теня• д̃невн• Да ся исправить мл̃тва• еѵ̃е ѿ ма̃а̃ ѡ̃ динтоямь и ѳ̃• мь часѣ• ѻ̃кте̃а Ръцѣмь вси• и прое, прежесщеннаа• Въ ср̃е великую, на оу̃трии а̃ллилуіа• въ гла̃ и̃• тр̃о г̃• Се жени• ка̃ г̃• с̃ѣ въ триѡ̃• ѱл̃ѡ н̃• и мл̃о, и начинае̃• и триѡ̃• г̃ла, козмы• ір̃мь по в̃• и тр̃ор на в̃і• и пакы• ір̃мь а̃• вкоу̃• по г̃• пѣ̃• к̃о̃ гла̃ д̃• въ з̃пе• Паче блудница беззаконновавь щедре• и слъзъ потоками никогдаже ти принесох• но млъчаніемь, мл̃яся припадаю ти• желая лобызати прѣч̃стѣи твои нозѣ• [я]ко да прощеніе мл̃ніа [я]ко вл̃ка даси долго зовоущю с̃п̃се• ѿ сквернъ дѣлъ моихъ избави мя:~ с̃вѣ г̃• На хва̃• самогласны д̃• гла̃ а̃• Тя д̃вч̃а с̃па• Мно̃гоцѣнно, Егда пріидеши• Ѡ іюдинос̃л• сла̃ і н̃ ѕ̃• Д̃нь х̃с на ст̃не а̃гл̃ны д̃• грѣшница• и г̃ гла̃ ѕ̃• Пріиде жена• Простре• И еще• с̃ти гле• Исплънихомся• И б̃жди свѣтло• сла̃ і н̃ и̃• Г̃и въ многыя• съвъкоупляе̃ а̃ ча̃ безъ сти̃сло̃ва
units.english_cohort_translation: *Exapostilarion thrice: ["Thy Bridal Chamber, O Lord, I behold adorned..."]. On the Praises: Idiomela 2, twice [on 4]: Tone 1: "Into the splendor of Thy saints how shall I enter..."; Tone 4: "He that had hidden his talent in the earth..."; Glory, both now, Tone 2: "In slothfulness of soul having fallen asleep, O Bridegroom Christ..." units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of Great Wednesday [Tone 4]:* Having transgressed more than the harlot, O Compassionate One, I have never offered Thee streams of tears; but in silence, praying, I fall down before Thee, desiring with love to kiss Thine all-pure feet, that Thou, as Master, mayest grant forgiveness of debts unto me who cry out: O Savior, deliver me from my filthy deeds!

On the Aposticha: Idiomela 4: "The sinful woman ran unto the precious ointment...", and 3 in Tone 6: "The woman came...", "She spread forth her hair...", "And yet another..."; we say the verses: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord..." units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion of Great Thursday, Tone 8:* When the glorious disciples at the washing of the Supper were enlightened, then Judas the ungodly, stricken with the love of silver, was darkened, and to the lawless judges surrenders Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold, thou lover of possessions, him who on their account hanged himself! Flee the insatiable soul which dared such things against the Teacher! O Lord Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!

units.verbatim_section_rubric: *At the 3rd hour of the day, they strike [the bell/semantron], and we chant the Third Hour, and together with it the Sixth and Ninth Hours; at which we say: "When the glorious disciples...", and Kontakion: "Taking the Bread..." After the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes are said, not in a chant, but simply [read]. Then the troparia of the Beatitudes: "The heavenly choirs...", "Pardon, remit, forgive...", "Our Father...", Kontakion: "Taking the Bread...", "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), and the Dismissal.*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Great Tuesday, at Matins:*[^585] *we sing "Alleluia" in Tone 8, and we say the Troparion thrice: "Behold, the Bridegroom comes..."
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *At the 7th hour of the day, we strike the great bells, and the priest vests, and we begin Vespers:*[^594] *without stichologia; "Lord, I have cried..." in Tone 2; and the priest performs the Proskomedia; Stichera on 10: Idiomela 5, Tone 2, chanted at Matins; Glory, Tone 6: "It were better for thee..."; Both now, Tone 6: "O brood of vipers..." Entrance with the Holy Gospel; readings of the day [Ex. 19:10–19; Job 38:1–23, 42:1–5; Is. 50:4–11]. After the readings... ...Little Litany; Exclamation: "For holy art Thou, [our God]..."; Trisagion ["Holy God..."]. Prokeimenon: "The rulers of the people [assembled together against the Lord and against His Christ]" [Ps. 2:2]; Verse: "Why did the heathen rage..." [Ps. 2:1]; Epistle to the Romans [sic; 1 Cor. 11:23–32]: "For I have received of the Lord..."; Alleluia: "Blessed is he that understands..." [Ps. 40:1]; Verse: "Mine enemies speak evil against me..." [Ps. 40:5]; Verse: "He that did eat of my bread hath lifted up his heel against me" [Ps. 40:9]; Gospel according to Matthew [composite Matt. 26:1–20, John 13:3–17, Matt. 26:21–39, Luke 22:43–45, Matt. 26:40–27:2]: The Lord said: "Ye know that after two days is the Passover..."; and the rest of the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.*

units.english_cohort_translation: *In place of the Cherubic Hymn: "Of Thy Mystical Supper [receive me today, O Son of God...]" thrice; that same hymn in place of the Communion Hymn, and "Let our mouths be filled..." And after the Prayer behind the Ambo, we go out from the church, and we perform the Washing of the Feet;*[^595] *and having returned, we make the Dismissal. And having entered into the refectory, we eat with olive oil, and drink wine; fish we do not eat. Compline we chant in the cells.*

Entrance with the Holy Gospel; readings of the day [Ex. 19:10–19; Job 38:1–23, 42:1–5; Is. 50:4–11]. After the readings... ...Little Litany; Exclamation: "For holy art Thou, [our God]..."; Trisagion ["Holy God..."]. Prokeimenon: "The rulers of the people [assembled together against the Lord and against His Christ]" [Ps. 2:2]; Verse: "Why did the heathen rage..." [Ps. 2:1]; Epistle to the Romans [sic; 1 Cor. 11:23–32]: "For I have received of the Lord..."; Alleluia: "Blessed is he that understands..." [Ps. 40:1]; Verse: "Mine enemies speak evil against me..." [Ps. 40:5]; Verse: "He that did eat of my bread hath lifted up his heel against me" [Ps. 40:9]; Gospel according to Matthew [composite Matt. 26:1–20, John 13:3–17, Matt. 26:21–39, Luke 22:43–45, Matt. 26:40–27:2]: The Lord said: "Ye know that after two days is the Passover..."; and the rest of the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.*

units.english_cohort_translation: *On Holy and Great Thursday evening: For the Holy Passions of our Master and God, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ:*[^596] *we strike [the bells] at the 2nd hour of the night. Having assembled in the church, we chant Matins, and sing "Alleluia" in Tone 8; Troparion thrice: "When the glorious disciples..."; and tapers are given unto the brethren. Then the Deacon says: "And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel..."*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: On Great Tuesday, at Matins:*[^585] *we sing "Alleluia" in Tone 8, and we say the Troparion thrice: "Behold, the Bridegroom comes..."
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *"Lord, have mercy" (thrice). Then the Deacon: "Wisdom. Stand upright." Then the [First] Gospel according to John [13:31–18:1]: The Lord said: "Now is the Son of man glorified..."; and we begin the Antiphons: 3 Antiphons are sung by the chanters standing in the midst of the church;*[^597] *Glory, both now, the canonarch sings the conclusion of these; and at the Sessional hymns we do not sit down. Then the [Second] Gospel [John 18:1–28]; likewise also the remaining Antiphons, Sessional hymns, and Gospels: after the 15th Antiphon and after the 6th Gospel [Mark 15:16–32], immediately the Beatitudes on 8.*[^598] *Then the Prokeimenon in Tone 4: "They parted My garments among them, [and upon My vesture did they cast lots]" [Ps. 21:18]; Verse: "O God, My God, look upon Me: why hast Thou forsaken Me?" [Ps. 21:1]; the 7th Gospel [Matt. 27:33–54], then read; and immediately Psalm 50; then the 8th Gospel [Luke 23:32–49].*

On the Praises: Idiomela 3, Tone 3, on 4: "Blindness falling upon thee...", "Two evils...", "Every member..."; Glory... ...Tone 6: "They stripped Me of My garments..."; both now: "I gave My back to scourgings..." The 10th Gospel [Mark 15:42–47]; "Glory to God in the highest..."; litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord..."; the 11th Gospel [John 19:38–42]; then we chant Aposticha: Idiomela 4: Tone 1: "All creation was altered with fear..."; and other 3, Tone 2: "Lawless people...", "Today upon the Wood...", and we say the verses: "They parted My garments among them..." [Ps. 21:18], "And they gave Me gall for My food..." [Ps. 68:21], "For God is our King of old..." [Ps. 73:12]; Glory, both now: "Lord, when Thou didst ascend..."; and the priest vests; the 12th Gospel [Matt. 27:62–66]. Then: "It is good to give thanks unto the Lord..." [Ps. 91:2]; Trisagion; Troparion, Tone 4

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: вся твар и ины г гла в людие
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Вся тварь.* и іны .г҃.* гла .в҃.* людіе нече стивіи.* на древѣ дн҃ь тѧ.* с҃. же гл̃емь.* ра здѣлиша собѣ.* и даша въ ꙗдь мою.* б҃ъ же цр̃ь нашь.* сл̃а і н҃.* г҃и въшедшю ти.* і п̃. оу́ же ѡблакаетсѧ.* еѵ҃ліе .в҃і.* та̃ бл̃го е испо вѣдати гви.* тр҃тое.* тро̃. гла .д҃.* Искоу пилъ ны еси ѿ клятвы законныа, чт̃ною си кровію пропныися на крьстѣ.* и копіемь прободесѧ.* бесъмрътіе источилъ еси члко сп̃се нашь слава тобѣ:~* ѻктеа. и ѿпоу:~*
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion of Great Friday, Tone 4:* Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with the spear, Thou hast poured forth immortality unto men: O our Savior, glory to Thee!

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Въслѣдованіе, часо̃ великаго пятка.* въ .г҃ и. ча дни.* поемь, .а҃. и .г҃. ча.* не ꙗкоже есть обычаи.* нѫ ꙗкоже въ оуставѣ оука зася.* тро̃ .а҃, го. ча̃.* гла .ѕ҃.* въ за оу́тра оуслыши гл̃а.* мѣсто̃.* г҃и ѡсꙋдиша тѧ
units.english_cohort_translation: *The Order of the Hours of Great Friday [Royal Hours]:*[^601] *at the 3rd hour of the day, we chant the First and Third Hours, not as is customary, but as indicated in the Typikon: Troparion of the First Hour, Tone 6: "In the morning hear my voice..."; in place of this: "Lord, the Jews condemned Thee to death..."*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ко̃ нарара* тр̃ .г҃. ча̃ гла .ѕ҃.* Токмо водроузи древо х҃е кр̃та твое́.* и основаніа подвижаша съмрти г҃и.* егоже бо пожре любовїю іꙗдь.* ѿпоу сти трепеща.* показалъ еси насп̃ніе твое ст҃ыі сласловим тѧ сп̃се б҃и помилꙋина.* во .ѕ̃ ча̃ дн̃ пое .ѕ̃ ча̃ и .ѳ̃.* тро̃ .ѕ̃ го ча̃ .г̃ .в̃.* сл̃ і н̃ іес дѣва .ѳ̃ го ча̃ .тро̃ .г̃ .и̃.* видѧ раз̃.* ко̃ нарара.* по ка е, ѣти.* ꙗмы ко іерл̃мѣ.* въ то днь.* съверше ныа лꙋр.* ин пресщ̃нныа не пріꙗхо стварꙗ.*

units.english_cohort_translation: *Concerning what is fitting to eat:*[^602] *As in Jerusalem, on that day neither the complete Divine Liturgy nor the Presanctified is received to be celebrated, nor do we set a table, nor eat, on that day of the Holy Crucifixion. If anyone is sick, or elderly and without strength, and unable to fast, let there be given unto him bread and water after the setting of the sun; for thus have we received from the ordinance of the Holy Apostles: not to eat on Great... ...Friday; for the word of the Lord, which He spoke unto the Pharisees: "When the Bridegroom shall be taken away from them, then shall they fast in those days" [Matt. 9:15].*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: Litany, and Dismissal. And we do not join the First Hour.*[^600]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On Holy and Great Friday: at the 10th hour of the day, Vespers without stichologia:*[^603] *"Lord, I have cried..." in Tone 1; Stichera on 6: then say 5 idiomela of the day: Tone 1, twice: "All creation...", and in Tone 2, one each: "People...", "Upon the Wood...", "Today beholding Thee...", Both now, Tone 6: "Today the Master..."; Glory, Tone 6: "Oh, how the lawless council...", both now, Tone 8: "A dread and marvelous mystery..." Entrance with the Gospel; "O Joyful Light..."; Prokeimenon: "They parted My garments..." [Ps. 21:18]; Verse: "O God, My God, look upon Me..." [Ps. 21:1]; then 3 Paremias are read [Ex. 33:11–23; Job 42:12–17; Is. 52:13–54:1]; Prokeimenon before the Apostle: "They laid Me in the lowest pit..." [Ps. 87:6]; Verse: "O Lord God of My salvation, I have cried day and night before Thee" [Ps. 87:1]; Epistle to the Romans [sic; 1 Cor. 1:18–2:2]: "The message of the Cross..."; Alleluia in Tone 5: "Save Me, O God, for the waters are come in unto My soul" [Ps. 68:1]; Verse: "Reproach hath broken My heart" [Ps. 68:20]; Verse: "Let their eyes be darkened that they see not" [Ps. 68:23]; Gospel according to Matthew [composite Matt. 27:1–61]: "When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders took counsel against Jesus..."; litany: "Let us all say..."; then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin..."; then: "Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord..."; then Aposticha: Stichera 3, Tone 2: "When from the Wood Arimathea took Thee down, Who art the Life of all...", with verses: "The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty" [Ps. 92:1], "For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved" [Ps. 92:1]; Glory, both now, Tone 5: "Thee Who art clothed with light as with a garment..."; then: "Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..."; after this, Troparion, Tone 2, thrice: "The noble Joseph..."; Dismissal; Compline in the cells.*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: Litany, and Dismissal. And we do not join the First Hour.*[^600]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On Holy and Great Saturday: at the 7th hour of the night, we strike the iron semantron, and begin Matins: "God is the Lord" in Tone 2, and we chant Troparion, Tone 2, thrice: "The noble Joseph..."; Glory: "When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal..."; Both now: "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women, the Angel standing by the tomb cried..."; Stichologia: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way" [Psalm 118], in tone... ...with refrains [Lamentations at the Tomb], in 3 Stases:*[^604] *after the 1st Stasis, the priest censes; and after the 3rd Stasis, there are sung the Resurrectional Troparia, Tone 5: "The angelic council was amazed..." Little Litany; then Sessional hymns of this day; after the reading, "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" is NOT said, but immediately Psalm 50. Canon in Tone 6: "By a wave of the sea...":*[^605] *the heirmos twice, and the troparia on 4; and again the heirmos once together. After Ode 3, Sessional hymn, Tone 1: "Thy tomb, O Savior..."; Glory, both now, the same. After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 2, Automelon: "He Who did not seek handwriting...":*

units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion of Holy Saturday [Tone 2]:*[^606] He Who shut up the abyss is beheld dead; and wrapped in myrrh and fine linen [the Holy Shroud], the Immortal One is laid in a tomb as one dead. units.slavonic_incipit: въ гробѣ полагаетсѧ ꙗко мр̃твь бесъмр̃
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в гробе полагается ко мртв бесъмр тныи жены
units.slavonic_diplomatic: въ гробѣ полагаетсѧ ꙗко мр̃твь бесъмр̃ тныи.* жены же придоша мѵ̃ромъ пома зати его.* плачюще горко и въпьюще.* сие ж ко та есть пребл̃венаꙗ събꙋта въ наже х҃с оусноу въ, и въскр̃се тридневенъ:~* въ свѣтлѣ сто. ст̃ыгъ.* нахва.* самогласны .д҃.* гла вторыи.* дн҃ь съдръжан:~*
units.english_cohort_translation: *Ikos: "In the brightness of Thy saints..." On the Praises: Idiomela 4, Tone 2: "Today He Who holds [creation] in His palm...", "What is this sight that is beheld...", "Come, behold [our Life lying in the tomb]..."; and another in Tone 6... ...and: "Joseph went in and asked for the Body of Jesus..." Glory, Tone 6: "Today secretly the great Moses prefigured this day..."; Both now: "Most blessed art Thou, [O Virgin Theotokos...]"; Great Doxology. The priest vests in full sacerdotal vestments;*[^607] *and he makes the Entrance with the Holy Gospel; he comes before the Holy Doors, and there stands awaiting the end of the Trisagion; and when the Trisagion is finished, he exclaims: "Wisdom. Stand upright." And they chant the Troparion: "The noble Joseph..." Then the priest enters: "Peace be unto all." Then the Paremia Troparion, Tone 4: "He Who holds the ends of the earth..."; then the Paremia of the day [Ezek. 37:1–14]; Prokeimenon before the Apostle: "Arise, O Lord my God, let Thine hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor for ever" [Ps. 9:33 (10:12)]; Verse: "I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart" [Ps. 9:1]; Epistle to the Romans [sic; 1 Cor. 5:6–8]: "A little leaven leavens the whole lump..."; Alleluia: "Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered" [Ps. 67:1]; Verse: "As smoke vanishes, so let them vanish" [Ps. 67:2]; Verse: "So let the wicked perish at the presence of God" [Ps. 67:2]; Gospel according to Matthew [Matt. 27:62–66]. At Matins, following the Gospel: Litany: "Let us all say...", and "Let us complete our morning prayer...", and the Dismissal.*

units.verbatim_book_heading: SYNAXARION OF THE TRIODION AND PENTECOSTARION :: Litany, and Dismissal. And we do not join the First Hour.*[^600]
units.verbatim_section_rubric: *On Holy and Great Saturday: at the 7th hour of the night, we strike the iron semantron, and begin Matins: "God is the Lord" in Tone 2, and we chant Troparion, Tone 2, thrice: "The noble Joseph..."; Glory: "When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal..."; Both now: "Unto the Myrrh-bearing women, the Angel standing by the tomb cried..."; Stichologia: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way" [Psalm 118], in tone... ...with refrains [Lamentations at the Tomb], in 3 Stases:*[^604] *after the 1st Stasis, the priest censes; and after the 3rd Stasis, there are sung the Resurrectional Troparia, Tone 5: "The angelic council was amazed..." Little Litany; then Sessional hymns of this day; after the reading, "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" is NOT said, but immediately Psalm 50. Canon in Tone 6: "By a wave of the sea...":*[^605] *the heirmos twice, and the troparia on 4; and again the heirmos once together. After Ode 3, Sessional hymn, Tone 1: "Thy tomb, O Savior..."; Glory, both now, the same. After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 2, Automelon: "He Who did not seek handwriting...":*
